overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific notice for its Aug 31 meeting and discussing minutes not listed on the notice; no violation by the Select Board or Board of Health; no further relief ordered.

allegations.summary: Aug 31 notice items 'Sign Operating Protocols' and 'Policy Changes' were alleged to be too generic to inform the public of the topics discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee’s August 31 meeting notice did not sufficiently advise members of the public that the Committee would be discussing these two topics.

allegations.summary: The joint Aug 18 meeting notice was amended on Aug 16 to add 'Public comment,' allegedly improperly.
allegations.key_passage: As the August 18 joint meeting was scheduled for 6:00 p.m. – more than 48 hours after the notice was amended – the Committee and Boards were free to amend the notice to add any topics they wished, regardless of whether the topics had previously been anticipated.

allegations.summary: At the Aug 31 meeting the Committee discussed approving prior-meeting minutes, a topic not listed on the posted notice.
Alleged that the Committee did not allow public participation at an Aug 31 meeting and has a policy of not always accepting public comment.
allegations.key_passage: As public participation is discretionary, these allegations would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Committee improperly delegated authority to the Superintendent to set COVID-19 protocols such as mask rules.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§  18-25.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Superintendent misstated her authority on the mask mandate and the Committee was slow to answer a public records request.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation

allegations.summary: Alleged an Aug 13 Superintendent email showed the Board of Health and other bodies coordinated COVID precautions outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As only one member of the Board of Health attended each of these meetings, we find no deliberation because there was no communication “between or among a quorum” of the Board of Health.

allegations.summary: Alleged the three bodies deliberated on the mask mandate outside a meeting because the chairs read identical motions at the Aug 18 joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Based on our review of the video recording of the joint August 18 meeting and extensive email communications, we are satisfied with Counsel’s explanation and find no other indication that a quorum of the Committee or the Boards deliberated outside of a meeting prior to the August 18 meeting.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Committee deliberated outside a posted meeting when the Chair spoke with one member about deferring the operating-protocols vote.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, a discussion between the Chair and one other member would not constitute deliberation, regardless of the content of the conversation, because the conversation was not “between or among a quorum” of the Committee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, as ordered for the Committee.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
